relu_triton_kernel.review_basis: Independent review checks the four sources and exact frozen evidence. Actual little-endian concatenation and bit extraction prove byte/word roundtrips; sequential four-byte stores equal an independent byte reference with a complete frame. A complete tagged LogicalView connects source-width input words and fp32 output words to byte loads. Under distinct logical names and full input/output interval separation, actual existing typed-grid success and wordSpec correspond to the independently defined byteGrid and byteSpec. Explicit B1024, N<2^31 and64-bit base/end domains give finite-address input assembly and every output-byte readback. Only the first min(N,1024) output words change; arbitrary prelaunch output tail remains. byteProgram is a total mathematical memory-effect projection: nonzero-pid loaded/result functions need not evaluate, so native load success/fault/poison or stepwise TTIR correspondence is not inferred. Native storage, allocator/layout, compiler/errors, host and concurrency remain open; three inherited numerical callbacks remain.

remaining_structural_obligations: RELU-B-S1: Native storage to mathematical little-endian byte memory. Real8-bit assembly/splitting and read/write relations are proved for a chosen total Nat-addressed byte map. Native device bytes, little-endian representation, pointer provenance, alignment, allocation/admission and source dtype dispatch remain to be related to that map. This is not merely a renamed logical cell, but it is not a native memory theorem.

RELU-B-S2: Native source/compiler and byte execution correspondence. The custom byteProgram is the source memory-effect projection with total byte reads, pre-store pid0 lane values and sequential4-byte stores. The nonzero-pid loaded/result functions can remain unevaluated; byte memory-effect success does not imply their native load success. The actual old logical source independently succeeds and its final tagged cells correspond to the byte result. This is an end-to-end representation proof, not a stepwise TTIR/extraction/native instruction theorem. Masked/unused values, access failures, poison, sanitizers and native addptr lowering remain open.

RELU-B-S3: Host-established layout and domain coverage. Distinct logical names and nonoverlapping contiguous physical byte intervals are explicit subtheorem premises; no runtime guard, empty_like freshness, tensor layout/stride or native wrapper property is inferred. Shifted/overlapping/misaligned layouts, N>=2^31, other block sizes, launch limits and native zero-grid behavior remain open.

RELU-B-S4: Remaining dtype, host/module and concurrent scope. Nine prior finite-word profiles are refined, with no additional dtype names. Prior fp64/fp8/error families, native host/harness/module stages, compiler targets and instruction interleavings remain required. Math-byte sequential grid success is not whole-original-program acceptance.

All previous dtype/error/host/harness/module obligations remain outside the explicitly added mathematical byte and finite-pointer relations. Numeric bounds, distinct logical names and full byte-interval separation are subtheorem premises, not original runtime guards or proved allocator freshness.

memory_model.masked_lanes: No source/native inactive-value, pointer admission, fault or poison claim. Only active result bytes and full memory effects are refined.
memory_model.numerical_carrier: BitVec32 Algebra outputs serialize exactly; numerical callbacks remain unproved native correspondences.

finite_address_domain.zero_N: No launched lanes in the logical model; native zero-grid behavior is not proved.
